title: 01 / The decision and intended user
sentences: Cambridge Storefront Opportunity helps the city's Community Development Department decide where to investigate vacant commercial spaces first.
The decision brief combines reported vacancies, approximate duration, and floor area to guide limited outreach and small-business support resources.
This presentation demonstrates the working website, its interactive comparisons, and the limits of what the evidence can support.

title: 02 / Read the decision brief
sentences: The dashboard uses the September twenty twenty-five storefront snapshot, not a live inventory of spaces available today.
The district chart compares counts and estimated average vacancy months, while the profile chart groups spaces by duration and size.
Boston food-license additions provide separate regional context; they are not a direct measure of Cambridge competition or customer demand.

title: 03 / Trace the data and protect privacy
sentences: The Method page explains collection from Cambridge, Boston, the Census Bureau, and the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
The project downloaded its source data on September twenty-first, twenty twenty-six, and generates the displayed measures through a reproducible Python pipeline.
Personal contact details are removed, and home addresses and coordinates from cottage-food permits are not retained in the deliverables.

title: 04 / Understand the measures
sentences: Cambridge reports a vacancy year rather than an exact date, so July is assumed when estimating vacancy duration.
The priority score multiplies the number of reported storefronts by their estimated average vacancy months within each district.
This combines vacancy volume with persistence, but it is an outreach ranking, not a forecast of profitability or investment returns.

title: 05 / Start an interactive comparison
sentences: On Explore, the initial view includes all commercial districts in the latest snapshot, with ninety-six reported storefront records.
The left panel controls district selection, reported floor area, and minimum estimated vacancy duration; the chart responds to these selections.
The Boston year controls affect the separate license context, so the two record counts should not be confused or combined.

title: 06 / Change the district selection
sentences: Here, East Cambridge is unchecked to demonstrate how a district selection changes the records included in the comparison.
The storefront count and chart update together, allowing an analyst to focus the discussion on the remaining commercial districts.
The selected filters also appear in the page address, making a particular comparison shareable with colleagues preparing the same briefing.

title: 07 / Compare districts with the same filters
sentences: Next, the Districts control switches the same filtered records into a district comparison without resetting the selection.
Bar length shows the number of storefront records, while color encodes estimated average duration, giving two views of vacancy pressure.
A district with many recent vacancies may need a different response from one with fewer spaces that have remained empty longer.

title: 08 / Investigate persistent vacancies
sentences: The minimum estimated vacancy is now set to thirty-six months, and the Vacancy profile view groups the remaining spaces.
This interaction narrows the question from all reported vacancies to spaces estimated to have been empty for at least three years.
The size bands help shape a targeted support proposal, but missing floor area and approximate dates still require case-by-case follow-up.

title: 09 / Inspect sources and download data
sentences: The Data page provides source links, access dates, field definitions, and downloadable files so another person can inspect the evidence.
The Cambridge snapshots, Boston licenses, and county industry statistics describe different places and periods and cannot be treated as interchangeable.
These downloads and the methodology note make the decision process reviewable, including its cleaning choices and the boundaries of each measure.

title: 10 / Identify the main findings
sentences: Central Square has fifteen reported vacant storefronts and ranks first on the combined count-duration score in the latest snapshot.
Seventy-nine of ninety-six records with a vacancy year, or eighty-two point three percent, are estimated to exceed twelve months.
The permit file contains fifteen cottage-food permits, with a median recorded submission-to-issue interval of twenty-six days; this does not establish expansion demand.

title: 11 / Turn findings into practical actions
sentences: First, prioritize an initial outreach cycle in Central and Harvard Squares, then review progress after ninety days.
Second, pilot small-space assistance for the thirteen observed spaces below fifteen hundred square feet estimated vacant for more than a year.
Third, offer an opt-in pathway for permitted cottage-food operators to explore shared kitchens or storefront testing, without assuming that every operator wants expansion.

title: 12 / Explain the limits and next evidence
sentences: These administrative records support prioritizing investigation, but cannot explain why a space is empty or prove that public support causes occupancy.
Year-only dates create uncertainty of roughly six months, and reported inventories can miss spaces or reflect changing collection practices.
Before funding decisions, add rents, lease terms, foot traffic, accessibility, and voluntary stakeholder feedback; use this website as a starting point for that investigation.
